The claim is **accurate**. 

The passage identifies "All's Well That Ends Well" as one of three Shakespearean problem plays written between the late 1590s and the first years of the 17th century (passage [1]). Passage [7] reveals that Rousillon Rupes, a scarp on the Uranian moon Titania, is named after a character from this same play and was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986. Therefore, the play (written in the late 1590s-early 1600s) temporally precedes the scarp's first imaging by nearly four centuries, making the claim factually correct despite the somewhat unusual phrasing of "happened before."
Was "All's Well That Ends Well" written before Voyager 2 first imaged Rousillon Rupes on Titania?

The claim is accurate. All's Well That Ends Well was written in 1604-1605, and Rousillon Rupes (a scarp on the Uranian moon Titania named after a character from this play) was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986. The play's composition predates the scarp's first imaging by approximately 380 years.
